newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures rise moderately at outset.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures rise moderately at outset.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures rose moderately at the near the outset but had clipped the biggest gains scored at the open.

June and new-lead-month September Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures each jumped to new all-time highs at the opening bell, hoisted upward by a rally in U.S. Treasury bond futures following weaker-than-expected consumer spending figures last month.
May retail sales fell 0.1 percent overall and ex-autos, both below forecasts for respective gains of 0.4 percent and 0.3 percent. April's declines were revised to bigger losses.

The soft May figures, the third consecutive monthly decline, further allayed concerns that demand might pick up enough to plant seeds of inflation and give the Federal Reserve an argument backing a rate hike at its July 1-2 Open Market Committee meeting.
The Dow 30 industrials sailed higher on the figures, although early weakness in over-the-counter stocks tethered futures to only-moderate gains.
Subsequent recovery in Nasdaq and high-tech stocks, which fell at first as analysts downgraded some computer component makers such as Intel Corp, let futures float up again.
The return higher saw September S&P 500s futures climb to an even higher all-time peak, this at 888.00, on an influx of big dealer buying, brokers said.
One floor technician said the contract rammed into a layer of resistance spanning the 887.00 to 888.00 area, although another extrapolated the next key at 888.75 level.
Futures also lost power as brokers watched NASDAQ stocks give up small gains and once again slip to the minus side.
Focus reverted to rolling of positions into the September S&P 500s futures and out of June, which goes off the boards next Thursday afternoon.
Open interest in June S&P 500s was 130,586 at Wednesday's close, and floor brokers said expiring contracts typically go off the boards with less than half that amount open.

Fair value Thursday for September S&P 500 futures stood at roughly 10.00 points premium. Arbitrage buy programs would require about a 10.90-point premium, and sell programs would need about a 9.10-point premium to cash.

At 1002 CDT/1502 GMT, Sept S&Ps rose 8.40 pts to 887.80, Midcap rose 1.60 to 288.70, Russell rose 1.35 to 394.85, Value Lines added 3.35 to 785.20, NYSE Composite up 3.65 at 462.40, Nasdaq fell 5.60 to 957.50, Nikkei rose 265.0 to 20,730.0.
